## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Unpleasantness at the Bellona Club" by Dorothy L. Sayers (Gutenberg 72855; 1928)

**Setting:** London, Nov 1928 (Armistice Day Nov 11 and after). Lord Peter Wimsey (detective), valet Bunter (ex-N.C.O., photographer), solicitor Mr. Murbles (soda-mint lozenges; of Staple Inn), Inspector Charles Parker (Scotland Yard; Evangelical; friend), Bellona Club (Piccadilly).

**Characters**
- General Fentiman ("Old Mossy-face"), ~90, Crimean veteran, wounded at Majuba; found dead in the smoking-room armchair by fire, Nov 11. Lived Dover Street flat; servant Woodward.
- Captain George Fentiman, grandson; gassed WWI, shell-shock, poor; wife Sheila (cashier at tea-shop; Finsbury Park flat; Mrs. Munns landlady, Mr. Munns, charwoman Mrs. Crickett). Owes MacStewart (Dougal MacStewart, moneylender; £1500 by 30th).
- Major Robert Fentiman, grandson, unmarried, Army, residuary legatee; later at Richmond rooms.
- Lady Felicity Dormer (née Fentiman), General's sister, married button-maker Henry Dormer (Sir Henry, Bart.; ~£700,000 fortune). Died Nov 11 at 10:37 A.M., Portman Square. Ward/companion: Miss Ann Dorland (£12,000 to her under will).
- Dr. Penberthy, Harley Street, ex-Army surgeon, gave certificate; secretly poisoned General with digitalin; engaged to Naomi Rushworth.
- Colonel Marchbanks (Bellona member; son killed Hill 60; dinner with Wimsey).
- Culyer (Club Secretary, one arm), Wetheridge (club grumbler), Tin-Tummy Challoner, Ormsby, Commissionaire Rogers, cloakroom man Williamson, hall-porter Piper/Weston (new), Fred (servant), Babcock (wine steward).
- Mr. Pritchard of Lincoln's Inn (Lady Dormer's solicitor; clerk spied).
- Lubbock (Sir James, analyst), Saunders, Dr. Horner.
- Marjorie Phelps (potter/sculptress, Chelsea studio), Salcombe "Sally" Hardy (Daily Yell reporter), Barton (Banner), Waffles Newton.
- Father Whittington (slum priest). Naomi Rushworth; Mrs. Rushworth; Walter = Penberthy.
- Taxi drivers: Swain (picked General at Portman Sq ~4:30 and took him to Penberthy's, Harley St) and Hinkins (took him from Harley St ~5:30 to Cavendish Sq/Regent's Park; "George" met; dropped at Bellona ~6:40).
- Nurse Armstrong; housemaid Nellie; housekeeper Mrs. Mitcham; footman William.
- "Oliver" = fictitious name Robert invented (taken from "Oliver Twist" on library book). Sleuths Incorporated: Wimsey's detective agency.

**Plot events in order**
1. Ch I: Fentiman and Wimsey in Bellona smoking-room, Nov 11 evening (Armistice). Colonel Marchbanks fetches Wimsey to General's chair; body stiff; Fentiman laughs hysterically ("He's been dead two days!").
2. Ch II: Penberthy examines; rigor established; body moved to room 16. Telephone cabinet "out of order" notice (Wetheridge complains). Lady Dormer dead 10:37 A.M. (maid at Portman Sq).
3. Ch III: ~10 days later, Murbles visits Wimsey with port (Cockburn '80). Explains Fentiman inheritance: General's will leaves ~£2000 securities to George; residuary to Robert. Lady Dormer's will: if General survives her, he gets bulk (~£700k); if he predeceases, Dorland gets bulk, £15,000 split between Robert and George. Time of death decides fortunes. Wimsey agrees to investigate.
4. Ch IV: Bunter's suit; Rogers, Williamson (General came in before 12:30, after 10:15; hat/coat on peg). Penberthy in bar: "dead a long time"; rigor passing off; knee-joint loose — Wimsey notes left knee swung loose.
5. Ch V: In library, Wimsey and Penberthy discuss leg; Wimsey photographs Club with Bunter (as "Twaddler" photographer). Wimsey finds note with figures (R, G, £150,000 to R., £300,000 to G.) in library blotter. Wetheridge lunch talk (telephone; soap; brother killed last day of War). Weston knows nothing.
6. Ch VI: Dover Street flat; Robert Fentiman; Woodward's story: General left ~10 AM Nov 10 by taxi? (Actually left Club at about 3pm after phone call from Lady Dormer's; went by taxi). ~9 PM phone call from "Mr. Oliver" saying General would stay the night. Wimsey examines clothes/boots (fragment of pile carpet from left boot, scratch/varnish), walking-stick prints; finger-prints taken (Fentiman, Woodward). Robert: "Oliver" tall, thin, grey hair, spectacles (Gatti's).
7. Ch VII: Adverts to taxi-drivers. Sir James Lubbock analysis: brown paint/varnish on boot. Wimsey visits George and Sheila in Finsbury Park; George's temper; Sheila's MacStewart debt; George's angry remarks on Dorland, "she paints". Wimsey buys Mrs. Munns's Johnny Walker at pub.
8. Ch VIII: Wimsey visits Miss Dorland (refused; note from her via servant); Pritchard (rude; "undesirable construction"). Parker traces "Oliver" call: made from Charing Cross public box (automatic, 9:13 P.M.). Parker identifies handwriting on notes = General's (Collins expert). Taxi-driver statements (Swain, Hinkins) — Hinkins says General went back to Bellona with "George" met in Cavendish Sq; "bear in mind what I have said."
9. Ch IX: Culyer complains. Wimsey gets Gatti's info. Georgie hired by Walmisley-Hubbard. Wimsey and George lunch at Gatti's; George complains of man following him; General told George about will in taxi (threatened cut-off over Sheila). Wimsey: "small thin man, hat down, rain-coat" the follower.
10. Ch X: Robert phones: saw "Oliver" at Charing Cross. Wimsey sets Sleuths watch. Wimsey visits Marjorie Phelps (Chelsea): Ann Dorland background (Ledbury; painting; Rushworths). Evening at Elephant (George Barnwell), fish-and-chips.
11. Ch XI: Sleuths report: Robert chases "Oliver" (Postlethwaite, retired manufacturer of Kew) to Southampton; Robert detained, released. Robert told to apply for exhumation (Wimsey dictates letter). Murbles: Pritchard offers compromise. Wimsey: "Bunter... Chambertin".
12. Ch XII: Parker dines. Theory: General died 10th evening in Bellona library, body put in telephone cabinet and carried to chair at 2-minute silence (Armistice Day). Oliver = "Oliver Twist" book in library. Wimsey, Parker, Murbles check: scratches in cabinet, nail, carpet. Clerk (Pritchard's) shadowing caught.
13. Ch XIII: Robert disappears from Richmond with suitcase; Wimsey's Paris telegrams; Wimsey, Bunter chase to Paris, Rome, Sicily. Exhumation at cemetery; Dr. Horner autopsy; George present; spooked.
14. Ch XIV: Robert returns; confesses: General told him of will in library around 8; Robert gave him digitalin? (Robert: General died in library ~8 PM; Robert hid body in cabinet, went to Charing Cross to phone). Lubbock: digitalin in viscera. Robert admits fraud; hits Wimsey; Wimsey punches Robert? (Ch XVII-XVIII: Robert/Wimsey dispute.)
15. Ch XV–XVII: Parker's investigation; Penberthy questioned (prescription of digitalin; amyl nitrate/brandy). Marjorie's party; Naomi engaged to Penberthy; Ann Dorland's studio; Nellie's account; Ann's paintings (portrait of sinister man = Penberthy). Nurse Armstrong.
16. Ch XVIII: George's breakdown; Mrs. Munns's dustbin bottle (digitalin tablet bottle). Robert and Wimsey row; Wimsey punches Robert. George goes missing; Walmisley-Hubbard car abandoned. Parker/Wimsey quarrel.
17. Ch XIX: Nurse Armstrong interview. Wimsey tea with Ann Dorland; she admits Penberthy engagement and affair; Penberthy's cruelty.
18. Ch XX–XXII: George found at Clerkenwell police station, confesses delusionally. Penberthy writes confession, shoots himself in library (Colonel Marchbanks leaves loaded revolver in drawer). Ann Dorland cleared as accessory.
19. Ch XXIII: Epilogue: Wimsey proposes to Marjorie Phelps (declined friend-level); Sheila/George recovering; Wetheridge complains of corked wine.

**Key facts/numbers:** Lady Dormer died 10:37 A.M. Nov 11. General's estate ~£2000; Dorland £12,000; Robert & George £15,000 split if General predeceased; ~£700,000 total. MacStewart debt £1500. Armistice: Nov 11, 1928; Nov 5 fireworks. Exhumation after ~3-4 weeks. Digitalin dose ~2 grains.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Linda Carlton, Air Pilot" by Edith Lavell (Gutenberg 44862; Saalfield, 1931)

**Characters**
- Linda Carlton (17–18, senior at Miss Graham's school, Spring City; blue eyes; sports roadster; loves planes; most popular girl in class; bracelet).
- Tom Carlton (father; rancher in Texas; absent-minded; roams; trouble with Mexicans; bought Arrow Sport "Pursuit" biplane as graduation gift). Mother dead.
- Aunt Emily Carlton (father's sister; raised Linda; fearful of planes; chaperone). Chauffeur Thomas.
- Ted Mackay (red hair, blue eyes, big, pilot instructor, mother/sister/family poor; father Mackay disgraced—stole from store, later ranch employee in Texas).
- Ralph Clavering (wealthy; Harvard; father millionaire oil; sister Kitty Clavering (pearl necklace, $50,000, from graduation)).
- Louise (Lou) Haydock (best friend; earrings; short hair; mother Mrs. Haydock).
- Maurice Stetson (wisecracker, Ralph's Harvard roommate), Harriman (Harry) Smith (engineer, takes interest in Linda), Dot Crowley, Jim Valier, Sara Wheeler, Sue Emery, Jackson Stiles, Joe Sinclair.
- Lieutenant Kingsberry (school head); H. B. Taylor (instructor, condescending); Sam Hunter (Ted's company colleague); Mr. Jordan (sales manager, Kansas City); Roger Stillman (eldest, 31; buys Pursuit); Dan Stillman (twin, borrowed Arrow, crashes? no—lost the plane); David Stillman (twin, sweet on Linda); Elsie; Anita; Mrs. Margaret Stillman; Mrs. Cates (ranch housekeeper); Cates (ranch helper); Dr. Winston; Dr. Lineaweaver (surgeon, St. Louis; vacationing in Louisiana seaport).
- Stolen necklace owner: Kitty Clavering; thief: man from Spring City school (unlicensed, shabby coupé); accomplice: Ted's father Mr. Mackay.

**Plot events in order**
1. Ch I (June, graduation): Linda's first flight with Ted Mackay (instructor) in old biplane; engine fails; both bail out by parachute; both land safely.
2. Ch II: Class-day (June, Miss Graham's school garden). Linda named most popular girl; bracelet. Class prophecy: Linda & Louise to marry rich men. Pink roses (from Ted, unsigned card). Linda wants to fly; Aunt Emily plans Lake Michigan resort (Green Falls) trip. Father didn't come.
3. Ch III: Picnic at lake (Grier's woods) with Ralph, Louise, Maurice; treasure hunt; Maurice's jokes. Father arrives, shows gift: Arrow Sport "Pursuit" with hangar. Linda ecstatic; father plans lessons; compromise: postpone Green Falls to August.
4. Ch IV: Dinner; father says Ted Mackay must be avoided (his father swindled him). Ralph Clavering decides to stay and learn flying too. Evening: Pursuit shown to friends; figure of man (red hair) spotted watching.
5. Ch V: Lessons at Spring City Flying School (Lieutenant Kingsberry). Father forbids Ted; H. B. Taylor assigned. Linda meets Ted, father cold. Ralph, Linda enrolled.
6. Ch VI: Weeks of training; loops; Ralph and Linda pass. Linda's last talk with Ted; he confesses sneaking over; says goodbye (job in Kansas City); thanks for flowers; gives business card. Ralph talks of Kit's necklace to be carried to Green Falls Midsummer Ball July 31 (Ralph suggests bringing "gun").
7. Ch VII: Flight to Green Falls (Linda, Ralph). Ralph loses white velvet box (necklace) out of sweater pocket during Linda's inside loops. They land in field; mysterious pilot (shabby coupé man, in "Waco") gives box to Ralph; Ralph pays him $20.
8. Ch VIII: At Green Falls, box opened: necklace missing (empty). Louise, Kitty, Maurice, Dot present. Linda offers to sell Pursuit. Linda & Ralph fly to hunt thief; find wrecked Waco; police ambulance; Linda sees Ted Mackay unconscious inside.
9. Ch IX: Ralph & Mr. Carlton suspect Ted; Mr. Clavering: insurance not cover air travel. Plan hospital visit.
10. Ch X: Ted in hospital (Spring City-area, 25 miles away): shot by thief in left arm; thief stole new company plane (Ted's). Father and Ralph visit, accuse Ted; Ted screams in defense of mother; nurse ejects them.
11. Ch XI: Linda's anxious day; father visits. Linda plans Queen Mab costume for ball. Father's parachute question; Linda reveals her jump (Lt. Kingsberry). Canoe party.
12. Ch XII: Linda phones hospital; Ted went home. Ralph says gas agent saw red-haired man with Waco. Quarrel; Ralph invites Linda; she refuses unless detectives called off. Louise arranges Harry Smith as Linda's partner. Linda flies scouting, nearly hits wires.
13. Ch XIII: Masque ball at Casino; Linda (Queen Mab) wins first prize; Ralph (King Arthur) for men; Ralph and Louise win dance prize.
14. Ch XIV: Linda & Louise swim; plan flight to Kansas City (Ted's company) and Sunny Hills (Colorado, Stillman's home). Mr. Jordan writes alibi letter: Ted at Winton Hotel lunch with sales-men; left for Buffalo ~3pm.
15. Ch XV: Sunny Hills (Stillman estate, 17 people). Roger, Elsie, twins Dan & David. Telegram: General/father "seriously hurt. Fly to ranch at once." Linda flies with Louise.
16. Ch XVI: Engine fails over wooded area; forced landing in weeds; Dan had borrowed Arrow the night before. Stranded; swim; find wrecked plane with two dead men (thieves; one red-haired = Ted's father) and necklace in coat pocket (cheap pasteboard box).
17. Ch XVII: Louise finds necklace; dead men; they camp.
18. Ch XVIII: Ted, at home, arrested by detectives; Sam Hunter arrives in plane with Mr. Jordan's alibi letter; detectives leave. Ted flies to Denver; Stillmans; Roger buys Ted's plane; Ted learns from German at shack (Nicht versteh) where girls are.
19. Ch XIX: Roger and Ted rescue Linda & Louise (Louise sits on Linda's lap in new plane). Father at ranch, critical; Dr. Winston; Dr. Lineaweaver needed. Linda flies Ted's plane? (Ted's plane?) Ted's ruined motor repaired; Linda flies back with Ted's plane (Pursuit repaired).
20. Ch XX: Ted reveals dead man was his father. Linda flies alone at night to Louisiana seaport, fetches Dr. Lineaweaver (Dr. Grayson's bungalow); dawn return; operation succeeds.
21. Ch XXI: Father recovers; Aunt Emily arrives; Louise's surprise; Labor Day Field Day at Green Falls: Linda wins airplane race (six loops; first with Pursuit, wins gold cup); receives medal for saving life. Ted and Sam perform stunts. Father forgives Ted; Linda's career begins. THE END.

**Key numbers/details:** Pursuit = Arrow Sport biplane; Aunt Emily; Linda's age 17 at graduation; necklace worth $50,000; Louisiana seaport; Denver field; Sunny Hills, Colorado; Labor Day field day; Midsummer Ball July 31; Linda's silver airplane gift; Queen Mab costume; Laura Ingalls 980 loops record reference.
